summary: Delayed client cookie sync prevents model-pin commit during canary window
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent quality regressions during a staged canary: some requests are routed to the fallback/compat variant despite an explicit model pin. Symptoms occur only while the canary prewarm completes and last for ~5-15s per cohort.

Impact:
- SparkLoop Media (dedicated) observed ~2.3% of user requests shifted to the degraded variant during canary windows, causing mismatched outputs and a small but measurable increase in support complaints.
- Affects live traffic in us-west for their reserved capacity pool.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated - reserved GPU pool (prod, us-west).
- Canary rollout: staged slices (10% -> 30% -> 60%).
- Clients use long-lived HTTP/2 connections with keepalive; edge sidecar performs cookie path normalization.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant session contains pinned model cookie (rw-pin) and orchestrator should commit pin atomically during canary handshake so requests continue to their pinned model.

Observed behavior:
- During slice transitions some sessions fail to commit the pin; orchestrator logs show pin_commit rejected with missing cookie. Edge logs show cookie update delayed by a downstream cookie rewrite step. Requests fall back to compat variant until cookie sync completes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated tenant with pinned model redwood/v1-7b-quant and start a staged canary release.
2) Open persistent HTTP/2 streams from a client simulator that reuses keepalive and performs reconnects every ~30s.
3) Trigger canary weight adjustment (10% -> 30%) and observe traffic for 60s around the weight change.
4) Monitor response model headers and orchestrator logs for pin_commit events.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:42:12.140Z serving-runtime[info] routed tenant=SL-931 -> fallback-compat variant=redwood/compat-3.4 reason=missing_pin
investigation: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Aisha Kumar): Confirmed customer traces with timestamped headers showing pin present on client side but not visible to orchestrator at commit time.
2026-03-10 12:30 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Replayed traffic in staging with an h2 keepalive emitter and reproduced missing cookie on the canonical handshake when edge rewrite latency >15ms.

Hypothesis: cookie rewrite step in the edge sidecar can race with orchestrator commit during canary prewarm; if the orchestrator receives the handshake before the cookie rewrite is acknowledged, commit aborts and fallback path is selected.
Checked correlated metrics: edge-cookie-latency spike aligned with canary slice adjustments. No quota or auth errors observed.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:00 - SparkLoop Support (customer): 'We see content drift for short windows during canary; it started after enabling cookie path hardening.'
2026-03-10 11:45 - Support (Aisha Kumar): 'Thanks, collecting logs and escalated to SRE. Can you share a minimal reproduction? Prefer same HTTP/2 client behavior.'
2026-03-10 12:55 - SRE (Diego Martinez): 'Reproducer ready in staging. Confirmed repeated pin_commit_failed entries paired with edge rewrite latency. Attaching a preliminary debug trace.'
2026-03-11 09:20 - Product Eng (Lena Horvath): 'If we see cookie rewrite delays, can we accept a fallback header during commit as interim? Need trade-offs on security/audit.'
2026-03-12 08:30 - SRE (Diego Martinez): 'Deployed a hotfix to orchestrator to tolerate cookie arrival up to 200ms after handshake (feature-flag gated). Beginning gradual rollout in us-west.'
2026-03-12 12:10 - SparkLoop Support (customer): 'Initial reports from our QA show the drift window disappeared after the hotfix rollout. Will confirm by EOD.'
root_cause: Race between edge sidecar cookie-rewrite acknowledgment and orchestrator pin_commit window: orchestrator required cookie present at handshake time and aborted commit when cookie absent; edge rewrite latency occasionally delayed cookie visibility leading to transient fallback routing.
resolution: Applied a three-part mitigation: 1) short-term: orchestrator now accepts a delayed cookie up to 200ms post-handshake behind a feature flag for the affected region. 2) medium-term: edge sidecar rewrite path optimized to acknowledge cookie writes faster and emit tracing for cookie sync latency. 3) long-term: add explicit session-handshake/ack step in the canary protocol and telemetry to catch pin_commit timing mismatches. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-coordinator/pull/459 was merged and rolled out to us-west with staged baking. Customer verified initial fix; monitoring shows fallback-rate reduced to baseline.
resolution_notes: Rollout plan: feature-flag enabled in us-west on 2026-03-12 08:30, monitor for 2 hours then expand if stable.
Post-deploy: added alert on pin_commit_failed rate >0.1% for dedicated tenants during canary windows.
Follow-up: update canary runbook and add cookie-sync latency section to the pinning-playbook confluence page.
Owner for follow-ups: Diego Martinez (SRE) and Lena Horvath (Product).
follow_up_items: 1) Instrument median cookie-write-to-orchestrator visibility latency and expose on Console per-tenant.
2) Add automated smoke test in preflight that simulates cookie rewrite latency and validates pin commits under h2 keepalive.
3) Revisit security review for accepting delayed cookie window; document audit implications.
